Backend API

RPP exposes a FastAPI backend in api/main.py. The Streamlit frontend uses this backend for account management, configuration persistence, and FITS file storage. A legacy backend still exists for compatibility, but the FastAPI service is the primary documented interface.

Authentication Model

  • Registration and login are initiated through JSON requests.

  • Authenticated routes use the current backend security layer from api/security.py.

  • The Streamlit frontend handles credential storage and request formatting through pages/api_client.py.

Core Endpoints

Health and Authentication

  • GET /health

  • POST /api/register

  • POST /api/login

  • POST /api/recovery/request

  • POST /api/recovery/confirm

Configuration

  • GET /api/config

  • POST /api/config

FITS Storage

  • POST /api/upload/fits

  • GET /api/fits

Behavior Notes

  • FITS uploads are written to user-scoped storage paths under rpp_data/fits/.

  • Configuration blobs are stored per user in the database.

  • Duplicate FITS uploads are rejected when the backend detects the same stored hash.

  • The backend returns schema-driven JSON responses defined in api/schemas.py.

  • Every successful POST /api/login (FastAPI) or POST /login (legacy) writes a timestamped line with the pipeline version to the service log, for example [2026-10-18 18:46:22] RPP v1.9.0 - User 'intern1' logged in successfully (FastAPI backend).

Configuration Persistence

The Save Settings button in pages/app.py serializes the whole analysis_parameters dictionary (every sidebar control, including Max Magnitude Error mag_err_max and Detector Gain effective_gain) together with observatory_data and colibri_api_key into a single JSON blob:

{
  "analysis_parameters": { ... },
  "observatory_data": { ... },
  "colibri_api_key": "..."
}

The frontend picks a persistence path from st.session_state.backend_mode. On the next login, pages/login.py fetches the blob and assigns its analysis_parameters / observatory_data entries back into session state (initialize_session_state in src/tools_app.py then fills in any missing defaults). Because the entire parameters dictionary is stored verbatim, every sidebar control round-trips without the backend needing to know its individual fields.

FastAPI backend (recommended)

  • Selected when backend_mode == "api".

  • POST /api/config with body {"config": { ... }} writes the blob to the users.config_json column of the SQLAlchemy-managed database.

  • GET /api/config returns {"config": { ... }}, or {"config": null} when the user has no stored configuration yet.

  • Authenticated with HTTP Basic; the client helpers are save_config / get_config in pages/api_client.py.

  • Implementation: api/main.py (save_config / get_config), model in api/models.py, schemas in api/schemas.py.

Legacy Flask backend

  • Selected when backend_mode == "legacy".

  • POST /save_config accepts {"username": ..., "config_json": "<json string>"} and stores the string in the users.config_json column.

  • GET /get_config returns the stored JSON string, or {} when none is set.

  • Authenticated with HTTP Basic. The server derives the username from the credentials via authenticate_request(); the username body field is ignored.

  • Storage: SQLite file users.db (users_dev.db when APP_ENV=development), created and migrated by backend.py.

  • Note: importing backend.py runs init_db() at module scope, and the module depends on flask / flask-cors; these are not part of the FastAPI install, so the legacy backend should be treated as optional.

Both backends store the blob as text in a config_json column, so no schema change is required when new sidebar parameters are added to analysis_parameters. Round-trip coverage for both paths lives in tests/test_config_persistence.py.

Main Backend Modules

api/main.py

FastAPI application, route definitions, upload handling, and response wiring.

api/models.py

SQLAlchemy ORM models for users, recovery codes, uploaded FITS files, and related tracking tables.

api/schemas.py

Pydantic request and response models used by the API.

api/storage.py

User-scoped storage-path generation for uploaded FITS files.

api/database.py

Database engine, session creation, and SQLAlchemy base setup.

api/security.py

Authentication helpers and dependency wiring for protected routes.

backend.py

Legacy Flask backend providing equivalent registration, login, recovery and configuration endpoints for compatibility with older deployments. Stores its data in SQLite (users.db) and requires flask / flask-cors.

Programmatic Use

For frontend-integrated usage, the simplest client surface is the helper layer in pages/api_client.py. For broader codebase entry points, see api_reference.rst for the surrounding module map.
